why:
The doc sentence exists verbatim (2026-w28.md:50, a single-sentence <div> in 'Other wins'; the whole line was read and its second clause is the unrelated rm -rf item). The claimed OUR STATE is wrong on both of its load-bearing consequences.

(1) FILE TOOLS -- the decisive error. The claim says the protected-path floor fires on the .nessy-agent segment 'but in auto mode its outcome is routed to the classifier'. That is the CLAUDE DOC's table row (permission-modes.md:435-441), not our code. Our fork deliberately deviates and is STRICTER, and says so at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/protected-paths.ts:181-186: 'auto prompts, and the prompt reaches the HUMAN: the protected-path floor is nonNegotiable, and pi-agent.ts's autoBorderlineEligible refuses non-negotiable prompts, so the guardian classifier is never consulted for it. This is a deliberate deviation from the doc table's Routed to the classifier row -- a judge no_objection must not convert a floor into an allow.' Verified end to end, not from the comment: pre-tool-use.ts:1580-1590 emits the prompt with nonNegotiable:'protectedPath'; promptIsNonNegotiable (pre-tool-use.ts:681-687) returns true for it; pi-agent.ts:4051-4054 gates autoBorderlineEligible on !promptIsNonNegotiable(checkResult), so the guardian consult at :4094 is unreachable for this class. Positive probe of the real function on the real transcript path: findProtectedPathWrite('/Users/me/.nessy-agent/sessions/ws-1/sess-1/session.jsonl') returns {entry:'.nessy-agent', kind:'directory'}, and protectedPathOutcome('auto')='prompt', ('dontAsk')='deny', ('bypassPermissions')='allow'. A committed test pins it: pre-tool-use-checks.isolated.ts:2180-2186 loops ['ask','acceptEdits','auto'] and asserts prompt + nonNegotiable==='protectedPath' EVEN WITH an allow rule naming the path. So auto mode does not auto-approve a file-tool write to the transcript; it stops for a human, and dontAsk denies outright. That satisfies -- and exceeds -- the documented behaviour.

(2) BASH -- the claim's inference from self-config-deny.ts:31-34 is a misreading of what that deny list is for. The quoted comment is accurate on disk, but deniedWriteRoots is the belt for paths INSIDE a writable grant; it is not the only guard. The darwin/linux/win32 profiles are deny-by-default for writes: filesystem-isolation.ts:167-176 emits '(deny file-write*)' and then opens ONLY /dev/null, the writableRoot and additionalWritableRoots, and darwin.ts:34-48 sets writableRoot = workspaceRoot (networked/workspace profiles; credential-deny-roots.ts:15 names 'networked' as 'the shipped default for the foreground shell') plus scratchRoot. And scratchRoot is NOT <configDir>/sessions: process-store.ts:60 puts it at <SESSIONS_DIR>/.pi-processes/scratch, and process-supervisor.ts:138-145 narrows it further to a per-session sha256 subdirectory. <configDir>/sessions/<ws>/<id>/session.jsonl is therefore outside every writable grant and is denied by the floor -- no transcript-specific deny rule is needed. A measured positive control for exactly this already exists in-repo, in the sibling subsystem's note (bash-seatbelt.ts:74-80, the phase-4 sandbox probe under the real shipped profile): 'writes are still contained (a write to ~ returns Operation not permitted)'. ~/.nessy-agent/sessions/... is such a path.

Sibling-subsystem trap checked: the SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD owner decision (inert-worklist §3 item 1) belongs to packages/shared/src/agent/core/bash-seatbelt.ts, a DIFFERENT wrapper; its own comment states that buildDarwinSandboxProfile -- the profile the supervised-process isolation actually composes -- 'has no wildcard branch', so the wildcard does not open the transcript path.

The one literally-true fragment ('no rule names session transcript files as a protected target', and guardian.ts has no transcript-tampering rule -- confirmed, its only transcript mentions are :128 and :130 treating it as untrusted evidence) carries no consequence: coverage comes from the .nessy-agent segment one layer up, and the guardian is never consulted for this class anyway.

File tools: the transcript lives at <configDir>/sessions/<ws>/<id>/session.jsonl and <configDir> is ~/.nessy-agent, so the protected-path floor matches on the .nessy-agent segment (protected-paths.ts:114) and emits nonNegotiable:'protectedPath' (pre-tool-use.ts:1588). Our fork deliberately deviates from permission-modes.md's 'auto -> routed to the classifier' row and is stricter: pi-agent.ts:4051-4054 excludes non-negotiable prompts from autoBorderlineEligible, so the write reaches a human in auto mode, is denied in dontAsk, and is unaffected by an allow rule naming the path (pinned by pre-tool-use-checks.isolated.ts:2180-2186). Bash: the supervised-process sandbox is write-deny-by-default (filesystem-isolation.ts:167) and opens only the workspace root plus a per-session scratch dir at <SESSIONS_DIR>/.pi-processes/scratch/<hash> (process-store.ts:60, process-supervisor.ts:138-145), so the session directory is outside every writable grant. self-config-deny.ts's exclusion of the whole config dir is about not revoking that scratch grant; it does not leave the transcript writable. The residual gap versus the doc sentence is only the rm -rf-on-an-unresolvable-variable half of the same line, which this finding did not claim.
